propositions: fsck does not detect the dirty-tree/stale-lock wedge class (tracked deletions, orphaned compaction leftovers, tmp-event files) that caused recent P0 wedges
doctor --repair does not have sanctioned recovery logic for the dirty-tree classes; current tooling (tracker-maintenance --clean) handles only stranded index and foreign worktree paths
fsck must classify git status output into three distinct tracker-dirty classes and emit separate JSON findings with counts and paths for each class

doctor --repair must heal dirty-tree wedges via two scoped write-lock windows (restore class-1 deletions via git checkout, quarantine class-2 leftovers, leave class-3 untouched) with backup ref and reconverge
repair operations must not delete files, must record a durable backup ref before mutations, and must release the write lock before invoking sync.reconverge
the write_lock is non-reentrant; doctor must not hold an outer lock during repair, and must acquire/release the lock around file-mutating steps separately from the reconverge call
